crop.notes: Left edge trimmed, losing the first letters of most lines; the column headline 'ALL ABOUT A BELT.' above the subhead is not in the clipping (visible on the page).

ocr.notes: Gist readable but many line starts lost to the crop and several misreadings (e.g. '$300' rendered as "$'", 'pawn-shop on Locust street' garbled).

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen's friends redeemed from a Locust Street pawn shop the belt Mike McCoole had kept after their first fight, to present it to Allen at his benefit.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Wednesday Morning, March 29, 1876, page 8.

facts.fact: At his first fight with Mike McCoole, Allen put up $300 against McCoole's belt in addition to the main stake; the mob broke up the fight and Allen lost the battle, the money and the belt
Allen's friends found the McCoole belt (the belt McCoole and Davis fought for), pawned by McCoole at a pawn shop on Locust Street, St. Louis, and redeemed it to present to Allen
A benefit for Allen was held at the Theatre Comique, St. Louis, on Thursday night, where the belt was to be presented to him

notes: The year of the McCoole-Davis belt fight is cut off at the left edge (ends in '6'); not recorded.
